findings.summary: The item 3 rewrite turns the doc's 'expected' non-moved lines into a hard 'must' rule. That fails every R5-R8 job and G1, so the plan changes the move rules, which is out of scope.
findings.evidence: Lines 227-228 now read: 'Any line not marked moved is listed in the job's report with its reason; the only expected ones are mod, use, pub use and visibility lines.' Other parts of section 5 require lines that are not moved and are none of those kinds: R5-R8 replace `return Ok(closing)` with `Flow::Stop` and add a struct whose fields carry locals (lines 249-253); G1 edits the WRAPPER constant in external_calls_guard.rs (line 1 allows it, lines 268-272) and the D87/D88 `paths` in introspect.rs (lines 261-263). The plan's new item 3 ('every line not marked moved must be a mod, use, pub use or visibility line') leaves no room for any of these. A job that follows its own R5-R8 or G1 instructions would fail item 3. The out-of-scope list says only the evidence rules may change, not what a move is allowed to contain. Fix: Keep the exceptions and make them checkable in the diff. For example: 'every line not marked moved is a mod, use, pub use or visibility line, or one of the changes this section names: the Flow::Stop and seam-struct lines checked by the R5-R8 bullets, and in G1 the guard constant and the D87/D88 paths of 5.2. Any other unmoved line fails the job.' Add a check that the rewritten item 3 still allows the R5-R8 and G1 edits.

findings.summary: An uncheckable criterion reported 'unmet' sets off a send-back the producer cannot act on, which wastes a producer run. The plan's claim that this 'surfaces the problem' overstates what happens.
findings.evidence: unmet_criteria counts any non-Met entry as unmet. producer.rs then sends the work back once (PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS), and only after that passes report_gaps to the verifier. The criterion's wording belongs to the reading, so the producer cannot fix it. After the send-back it may either invent a file, which the new text forbids, or re-mark the criterion met. Fix: Keep 'unmet' if you want, but describe the cost honestly in the risks: one wasted send-back, after which the verifier sees the gap in report_gaps. Optionally have the producer's evidence begin with a fixed phrase such as 'not checkable by the verifier' so the send-back and the verifier can recognise it.
findings.location: Plan decision 3 / step 4; crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs 519-578; run/send_back.rs unmet_criteria

findings.summary: The item 5 text and the open question rest on the claim that 'a stored before count cannot be rechecked'. That claim is doubtful, and the plan does not need it.
findings.evidence: The base commit exists in the candidate's git repository: the working-directory text at briefs.rs 656-657 describes a one-commit repo holding the base. A read-only `git grep -c <pattern> <base>` could therefore recompute a before count. The plan's real argument is stronger anyway: a `git diff -U0` that shows no old-path line added or removed outside moved blocks already proves the counts are equal. Fix: Drop the 'cannot be rechecked' sentence from the doc text. Say instead that the diff check makes the before and after counts equal by construction, so no count needs to be stored. This also brings item 5 closer to criterion 3's wording about counts.

findings.summary: Criterion 3 says the counts are to be 'put in the snapshot (a committed file or test)'. Item 5 as planned requires no counts at all, so a literal-minded verifier may judge criterion 3 unmet.
findings.evidence: The plan flags the conflict with items 1, 4 and 7 as an open question, which is the right move. As planned, the demonstration still does not show the literal wording of criterion 3. Fix: Have the producer report quote the item 5 sentence that ties the old-path Grep to committed tests and the diff check, so the verifier can map it to criterion 3 directly. Also keep the open question.

summary: I checked the plan's code references by reading the snapshot. They hold: reader_brief puts CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE at line 2425, inside the rules section, followed by the conditional `# What the verifier can run` block. The rules-section tests split at `\n# `, so a new `# Checkable criteria` section between the two leaves READING_RULES and its length tests untouched. In the producer brief, criteria_check_section is called at line 686. The test helpers exist: reader_inputs has a non-empty verifier_can_run, and producer_briefs_say_what_the_verifier_can_see is at line 2710. The D87/D88 test is at introspect.rs:1707. CHANGELOG has an `[Unreleased] / ### Added` section. Both brief demonstrations call the real production entry points, use literal phrases, and would fail without the change. The brief half of the plan is sound. One major problem is in the structure-pass.md rewrite. The new item 3 makes 'every line not marked moved must be a mod, use, pub use or visibility line' a hard rule. That drops the room the doc gives for the R5-R8 control-flow changes and the G1 guard and D87/D88 path edits, so jobs that follow section 5 would fail it. That changes the move rules, which are out of scope. Smaller points: an uncheckable 'unmet' criterion costs a send-back the producer cannot act on, and the 'stored before count cannot be rechecked' justification is doubtful and not needed. Revise item 3 to keep the named exceptions as checks the verifier can read in the diff.
